I'm weighing whether to send Badajoz's knights alone for speed against Toledo's garrison, since mixing in spearmen would slow the attack without changing the defender's strength meaningfully. I need to work through how the counter-attack mechanics apply when spearmen defend against knights.

Since Toledo's garrison is majority spearmen, and spearmen counter knights, sending knights alone would actually favor the defender with a bonus rather than help us. Archers counter spearmen instead, so I'm considering routing Salamanca's archer-and-knight force toward Toledo directly, since Salamanca connects straight to Toledo on the road network.

Testing the numbers: Salamanca's 2 archers alone only reach an effective attack of 6 with the counter bonus, still short of Toledo's defense of 10. Badajoz's 9 spearmen give 9 attack against 10 defense, also a losing tie, and adding knights to that mix would just trigger the spearman counter-bonus against us since spearmen are the dominant type in the combined force.

So the real winning move is sending Badajoz's full army—9 spearmen plus 2 knights—where spearmen remain the majority type but don't trigger any counter bonus either way against Toledo's spearman defenders, giving a flat attack sum of 17 versus defense 10. That clears Toledo easily. Now I'm looking at Salamanca's route to Madrid, checking whether its archer-majority force of 2 archers and 1 knight (attack power 8) gets a counter bonus against Madrid's spearman garrison.

Since archers counter spearmen, that bonus turns the effective attack into 12, comfortably beating Madrid's defense of 10. I'm noting that the reported "attack power if all sent" values seem to be raw sums without counter multipliers, confirmed by matching Badajoz's 17 exactly—so I need to apply counter bonuses manually depending on each target's garrison type.

Checking Cordoba next: sending 4 archers and 1 knight from Sevilha gives 12 raw power, and since both attacker and defender are majority archer, there's no bonus to apply—still 12 beats the defense of 10, so it's a clear win without needing any counter advantage.

For Vigo, defense 8 with 3 spearmen garrisoned, Porto's available force is only 2 spear+1 knight, giving power 6, no bonus since matching spearman types—6 is short of 8, so that attack fails. Sending just the knight alone would actually be worse since spearmen counter knights, so I'll skip Vigo this turn and consider building up more troops at home villages first.

I'll focus on producing cheap spearmen using surplus wood/iron at Lisboa, building two spearmen there, and I'm weighing whether Santarem's troops should stay home to defend while its resources go toward building an archer instead.

Santarem and Evora each have similar wood/iron surplus, so I'll build one archer plus one spearman at both to use resources efficiently. For Coimbra, since we're not pulling its troops for the attack, I'm calculating whether its larger wood/iron stockpile can support two archers instead.

Deciding to skip sending Porto's troops to Vigo this turn and just build there instead. For Badajoz, after sending its attacking troops, I'll use remaining resources to build an archer and spearman for variety. At Faro, I'll keep the existing knight home for defense and similarly build an archer and spearman with the available resources.

Salamanca has no resources left to build since it was just conquered and all its troops are heading to Madrid. Sevilha, after sending its attack force to Cordoba, has enough leftover wood and iron to add an archer and spearman too.

Rounding out construction with archer/spearman pairs at Coimbra, Faro, and Sevilha, plus a knight at Porto and Badajoz. That's a solid enough plan overall—time to write it up along with the depoimento.

I'm tracking the back-and-forth control of Madrid and Toledo with King B, and calculating whether my marching force of spearmen and knights can overcome Toledo's garrison of two archers when it arrives next turn.

Working through the counter-triangle mechanics, since archers counter spearmen and my army is spearman-majority, the defending archers likely get a 1.5x defense bonus against my attack, which changes the odds of taking Toledo back.

Now I'm shifting focus to what to do this turn: with Salamanca empty and Cordoba freshly conquered with a small garrison, I notice Cordoba actually borders Madrid directly on the road network - so instead of routing through Salamanca, I can send Cordoba's available archers and knight straight at Madrid, which just fell back into enemy hands.

Checking the matchup: Madrid's garrison of 1 archer and 1 knight ties, and tiebreak rules mean archer wins the tie as defender majority. My force of 2 archers and 1 knight is also archer-majority, so this is a same-type matchup with no counter bonus either way - straightforward power comparison, 8 attack against Madrid's 5 effective defense.

But sending all 3 units from Cordoba leaves it completely undefended, which is risky since it borders two enemy territories. Sending only 2 archers drops attack to 4, which loses against defense 5 - I need the full 3-unit force to actually win this fight.

I'll accept the Cordoba risk and send all 3, but plan to reinforce it right after with Sevilha's spare troops - 1 spearman and 1 archer that can reach Cordoba in a single turn. That should stabilize the border once the attack succeeds. Now I'm thinking about whether to also push toward Vigo.

Vigo is neutral with 3 spearmen and defense 8. If I send Porto's 2 spearmen and 2 knights, my attack comes out to 10 - enough to win since my majority defaults to spearman on the tie, matching the defender's type with no counter bonus either way. That's a solid opportunity to grab another village this turn.

I also notice Salamanca has zero troops, which is a serious vulnerability since it borders two enemies. With 30 wood and 20 iron there, I can build two spearmen using all the wood, which is cheap and gives it at least some defense. I'll plan similar build orders for other villages too, like putting Lisboa's resources toward knights, to keep growing the army.

Porto builds a knight since resources still get produced regardless of troop movement. Badajoz and Faro can each fit an archer plus a spearman using their wood and iron exactly.

Sevilha, despite already sending troops to Cordoba, still has full resources to build an archer and spearman too. Cordoba has zero resources since it was just captured so no build there, while Salamanca fits two spearmen with its wood.

Now I'm working out the troop sends: Porto sends spearmen and knights to attack Vigo, and Cordoba sends archers toward Madrid.

I'm sending 1 knight to reinforce that attack, plus a spearman and archer from Sevilha into Cordoba. Badajoz's marching force to Toledo stays untouched, and I'll keep its remaining home troops for border defense rather than reinforce Toledo late. I'm also considering pulling interior troops from Lisboa, Santarem, Evora, Coimbra, and Faro toward the exposed Salamanca or Badajoz front.

Salamanca has zero defense, so I want Coimbra's remaining spearmen and archers to reinforce it, though mixing unit speeds means the whole group moves at the slowest pace, taking two turns instead of one. I'll just accept the slower arrival since reinforcement value matters more than speed here.

Evora's home guard, with its knight, spearmen and archers, should reinforce Badajoz too, since that border faces potential counterattack once the marching forces move out. Santarem also borders Badajoz and can reinforce in just one turn given its fast unit.

Faro's small garrison of spear, archer and knight can march toward Badajoz as well, though I'm sending a lot piecemeal now. Still, consolidating strength at Badajoz makes sense since it's the active front holding troops that just took Toledo, and I want to guard against retaliation there before finalizing the order list.

For this turn's fresh orders, I'm scanning garrisons: Badajoz (def15), Salamanca (def18), Sevilha stands out as very weak with only 1 knight and def3, while Burgos and Madrid are both getting reinforced by inbound enemy armies. I'm also weighing whether Coimbra's 4 knights could retake Salamanca, but with an attack of only 16 against defense 18 and archers likely countering knights there, that assault looks risky too.

Since Coimbra will lose its knights attacking Salamanca, it'll be left weaker, so I should route Porto's knights to Coimbra as reinforcement afterward to keep it defended.

Lisboa has spare knights and no border threat, so I'll send them to backfill Santarem once its own knights depart to attack Badajoz, keeping that garrison covered too.

Evora's 2 knights are in a similar spot—send them to Faro, since Faro's defense will drop sharply once its spearmen leave for the Sevilha attack. Then I need to work out village build orders, balancing wood/iron production against troop upkeep for each settlement.

The listed wood/iron figures are current stock, with production applied separately per turn, so I'll spend from what's already available. Going village by village, I'm figuring out max affordable troops given each one's current wood/iron—Lisboa has 30 wood and 60 iron, enough for one knight (30w/30i), leaving 30 iron spare, though I could alternatively build two spearmen instead since those only cost 15 wood each.

For Santarem with 30 wood and 80 iron, the wood cap of 30 means only a single knight build is possible per village regardless of surplus iron, since the knight uses up all available wood at once.

Going through the remaining villages: Evora, Coimbra, and Porto each get 1 knight built with their 30 wood. Faro stands out though with 90 wood and 150 iron, allowing 3 knights to be built there using 90 wood and 90 iron, leaving 60 iron idle. Vigo with 30 wood and 50 iron also gets just 1 knight, with leftover iron unused.

For attacking assignments, I'm sending Faro's 15 spearmen to Sevilha, Santarem's 4 knights to Badajoz, and Coimbra's 4 knights to Salamanca. For reinforcements, Porto's knights go to the now-empty Coimbra, Lisboa's knights go to Santarem, and Evora's knights go to the emptied Faro. Vigo holds its 27 troops back for defense.
